assembly_instructions: A two-metaphor diorama on a single 21 m × 15 m concrete plot, modelled at 1× (human-readable scale). LEFT HALF: a recognizable suspension-style bridge — a flat steel deck carried on four 3 m concrete cylinder piers, two 7.4 m steel towers with cables, and side railings — but the centre span between pier 2 and pier 3 has FAILED: one deck segment dangles from pier 2, another from pier 3, and a third has fallen flat into the gap. RIGHT HALF: five short white plinths in a row; the centre plinth carries an enormous 2.5 m pile of gold bars and coins towering far above a person, while the other four plinths hold only one or two coins each. Build the bridge first (piers → decks → railings → towers → cables), then the pedestals, then stack the coins. Connections are physical attachment only.

info.summary: A diorama pairing two concrete metaphors on one ground plot: a well-built bridge whose middle span has collapsed, and a row of pedestals where one holds a towering pile of coins and gold bars while the rest hold almost nothing.
info.description: The left half is a suspension-style road bridge — a steel deck on four concrete piers, two towers, cables and railings — built to look entirely ordinary, yet the centre span between the second and third piers has failed: one deck segment hangs off each surviving pier and a third lies crumpled in the gap, with a snapped cable still attached. It is meant to read instantly as 'a real bridge that nonetheless breaks'. The right half is five identical 1 m display plinths in a line; the centre plinth bears a 2.5 m stack of nine gold bars and coins, rising well above adult head height, while the four neighbouring plinths carry just one or two flat coins. The deliberate visual imbalance — a structure that fails despite looking sound, and resources piled almost entirely on one party — is the entire message of the scene.
